html:
The Battle of Tuyutí was fought on 24 May 1866 in the marshes of southern Paraguay, when the Paraguayan army attacked the camp of the Brazilian, Argentine and Uruguayan allies. It was the largest pitched battle in South American history.

Francisco Solano López hoped to destroy the allied army that had crossed into Paraguay. His columns struck through swamps and woods but were cut down by allied artillery. In a few hours Paraguay lost much of its best army, killed or wounded.

The allies were too weakened to follow up at once, and the war dragged on for four more years. Paraguay won a defensive victory at Curupayty in September, but never again could it attack in force. Tuyutí marked the turning point of the War of the Triple Alliance and the start of the long agony that ended at Acosta Ñu.
